title: Clocked rounds and head control
statement: Let $e$ be an injection from $\\{\\mathrm{false},\\mathrm{true}\\}$ into an alphabet $\\Gamma$, let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine with state set $S$, and let $\\mathrm{stopAt}:S\\to\\{\\mathrm{false},\\mathrm{true}\\}$. Fix an input word $x$, a configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, and a state $q\\in S$ such that $c$ has state $q$; let $w$ be a Boolean word, $ct:\\mathbb Z\\to\\mathrm{Option}(\\Gamma)$ a tape, and $cp\\in\\mathbb Z$. Assume that for every integer $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$, the tape cell $ct(cp+p)$ contains the symbol of $w$ at offset $p$ after encoding by $e$ (with blank cells represented by absence). Let $n\\in\\mathbb N$ be at most the integer represented by the binary digits of $w$, and suppose the run of $M$ from $c$ is not stopped at any time $v<n$. Then, after $\\mathrm{counterOverhead}(w,n)+n$ steps, the clocked machine reaches the clock configuration whose body component is the configuration of $M$ after $n$ steps, whose clock tape is patched with the encoded counter word for round $n$, and whose clock head is at $cp$. The run segment up to that time avoids the exit states before its endpoint and keeps the clock head in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$ throughout. Moreover, at every time $u\\le \\mathrm{counterOverhead}(w,n)+n$, the clocked configuration consists of a clock state, the body configuration of $M$ at some time $v\\le n$, a tape, and a head position in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$.
